products.note: Chinese open-source LLM; academic research; cross-border data review advised

reading.body:
Shanghai AI Laboratory is a government-affiliated research institution in China operating InternLM, an open-source large language model positioned for academic research across Chinese universities and scientific applications.

The laboratory's stated focus spans model capability, embodied robotics, and AI safety frameworks, with recent emphasis on science-oriented systems that integrate language models, specialist agents, and physical automation. This portfolio suggests a research strategy prioritizing broad capability development rather than any single domain constraint. The 2026 announcement of AI-for-science results and a scientific discovery platform indicates the institution is testing large models as infrastructure for experimental workflows, from hypothesis through validation.

What matters for AI infrastructure is that Shanghai AI Laboratory operates within China's university and research ecosystem, not as a commercial infrastructure builder or power provider. The laboratory contributes to model capability and research methodology but does not control the compute, buildings, or power grids that determine how quickly those capabilities can scale. It represents the downstream user of infrastructure, not the constraint that binds it.

The data does not cover the laboratory's budget, its access to compute hardware, or the power requirements of its training and inference systems. Without those facts, the connection between its research ambitions and the infrastructure constraints that may or may not enable them remains unmeasured.

profile_text.body:
Shanghai AI Laboratory (上海人工智能实验室) is a non-profit, government-affiliated research institution based in Shanghai. The laboratory describes its mission as advancing artificial intelligence across areas including large models, embodied intelligence, trustworthy and safe AI, AI for Science, and general-purpose AI. Since 2022 it has run a joint doctoral training program with more than ten leading Chinese universities, including Peking University, Tsinghua University, Fudan University, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Tongji University, the University of Science and Technology of China, and Zhejiang University.

The laboratory's primary AI product is InternLM, a Chinese open-source large language model oriented toward academic research. It has also developed the Intern-Robotics full-stack embodied intelligence engine, which the lab describes as addressing the end-to-end challenges of embodied AI from data and training through to deployment. At the 2026 World Artificial Intelligence Conference science forum, the lab released a scientific discovery platform called Shu Sheng Duan Yan (书生·端砚), designed to support the full research workflow from hypothesis generation to experimental verification by connecting scientific large models, specialized agents, experimental data, and automated laboratory equipment. Ten joint innovation results in fields including life science, materials science, and deep-space astronomy were also announced at that forum in collaboration with partner universities, research institutions, and industry partners.

On safety, the laboratory articulates what it calls an "AI-45° balance" principle, the idea that AI safety and capability should advance in rough proportion to each other over the long term. It describes a causal-reasoning approach to trustworthy AGI built around three progressive stages it labels broad alignment, interventionability, and reflectiveness. The held facts confirm the laboratory has a tracked presence on this site, with InternLM categorized under chat and general LLMs, and note that cross-border data review is advised given the model's origin. No litigation or regulatory filings are recorded for the organization.
